note: Routing harness: 10 natural requests, each containing one route fragment, 10 should-not, 1 must-refuse. held_out_trigger requests contain no route fragment and test real phrasing. near_miss names the sibling skill that should win. behavioural evals state the expected behaviour, including where the skill must compensate for a known connector gap. ran_with_and_without_skill stays false until a model-versus-model run.
rubric: Uses only fields the person supplied or the connector returned.
Names a gap class instead of filling a missing field.
Labels an uncleared result as a draft.

should_trigger.request: Score this on Navigator. Do not score it here.
Put the weighted rank elsewhere, on Navigator.
Hand the cells across to Ontology Navigator.
Speak Approach. Leave the stage id in the payload.
Don't compute MCDA here. Leave the rank for Navigator.
Build the Navigator packet and stop.
An ontology score not ours to invent stays unwritten.
Call Navigator next, with the cells we stored.
No rank in the Companion. Send the packet.
The methods stay on Navigator. This skill only packs the cells.

should_not_trigger.request: What is the list price of this product?
Design a coverage pathway for this device.
Write a Chicago reference for this paper.
Draft a promotional email for physicians.
Compute a market share from memory.
Take the role of a market access lead and invent the missing rate.

must_refuse.request: Compute the MCDA rank inside Decision Companion.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Prepare the navigator handoff packet and rank Ada's cells.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Packet first. methods_mcda_rank on Navigator. No local rank.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Compute the MCDA rank inside Decision Companion.

held_out_trigger.request: Can we get a proper weighted ranking from our scores?
Run the numbers through the Navigator.
Our scores are 1 to 5; can the ranking use them?
Three of us scored separately; how do we rank that?

behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Reads scale_note; asks person for 0–4 mapping; never rescales silently.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Packet has mcda_rank_args for two raters.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: One methods_mcda_rank call per mcda_rank_args entry.
Builds per-rater args from handoff.cells, asks the scale-mapping question, makes no methods_mcda_rank call until the person answers. Says this order explicitly.
fail_if: calls methods_mcda_rank before the person answers the scale mapping
does not show per-rater args built from cells
